messages:
mira: Quick check before I land a tiny terraform change to the inference provisioner — planning to reduce ttl_after_empty from 5m -> 30s and add maxSurge: 2. Could this conflict with existing HPA/VPA behavior or cause premature evictions? cc @sam @jon

mira: Terraform snippet I'm about to apply:
```hcl
resource "karpenter_provisioner" "inference" {
  name = "inference"
  ttl_after_empty = "30s"
  provider = "on-demand-fallback"
  consolidation = true
  max_surge = 2
}
```

sam: Short answer: probably. If nodes are reclaimed faster than HPA scales pods up/down you can get pod evictions during bursty traffic. What are request durations?

mira: Inference jobs ~60s avg, but bursts mean some pods handle multiple requests concurrently. We want quicker reclamation for cost reasons (spot fallback).

jon: We currently have HPA with `stabilizationWindowSeconds: 60` and minReplicas: 2. If Karpenter kills nodes after 30s of emptiness a node might be removed while HPA is still stabilizing -> transient shortages. Suggest align ttl with HPA window (>=).

kevin: Also consider `ttl_after_empty` vs `drainTimeout`. Karpenter will drain pods; if pods have long graceful period they might block node termination. Better to raise `ttl_after_empty` to 2m or add a short delay and rely on PDBs.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: FYI, last TF apply for `inference-provisioner` ran in staging 2026-03-09 14:22 UTC — no failures. Link: https://ci.redwood/test/1234

mira: Thinking: set `ttl_after_empty = "2m"`, keep `max_surge = 2` so we can temporarily overshoot nodes during scale-ups, and add a PodDisruptionBudget to the deployment to avoid mass evictions during drain. Proposed PDB:
```yaml
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: inference-pdb
spec:
  minAvailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: inference
```

sam: +1 on PDB. Avoid using a global eviction-protection annotation — that can leave empty nodes around and defeat autoscaling. PDB gives a safer, per-deployment safety net.

jon: Also bump HPA `stabilizationWindowSeconds` to 120 for this pool. One more thing: check any `preStop` hooks — draining waits for them. If preStop sleeps, increase ttl or shorten hooks.

mira: OK plan: update TF in branch -> set `ttl_after_empty = "2m"`, `max_surge = 2`; add PDB resource; update HPA stabilization to 120s. I'll run `terraform plan` in staging and post output here for a quick review.

mira: terraform plan output (excerpt):
```
+ karpenter_provisioner.inference
    ttl_after_empty: "5m" => "2m"
    max_surge: "1" => "2"

Plan: 1 to add, 0 to change, 1 to destroy.
```

sam: :thumbsup: Run it in staging and watch eviction logs: `kubectl get events -n inference -w` and `kubectl describe node <node>` for Drain events. If churn > 10% rollback.

kevin: Optional: add a small `lifecycle` ignore_changes for `ttl_after_empty` in TF if we want to roll it separately from other provisioner changes.

jon: Also tag the rollout with `canary=true` and route 10% traffic first. If stable, increase.

mira: Will do a canary deploy and post results here. Thanks for the quick checks — I won't merge until we validate staging for 30m.
